answer: Reputation-Weighted Work Ledger. Each new agent identity must complete a costly anchor task whose result is publicly verifiable before it can transact. Honest agents build a persistent history that acts as a ledge: past verified work raises their standing and lowers future task costs, while cloned identities start each time from zero cost savings. To reach the summit of high-value contracts, an identity must accumulate that history, which cloning cannot shortcut. Attacker cost: full compute and time for every clone's anchor task, paid repeatedly with no transferable credit.
